findings.title: 36 % of the recorder payload per cycle is series-shaped or byte-identical on repeat
findings.claim: Of the 9,512 bytes of entity attributes written to the recorder every optimisation cycle, 1,753 B are series-shaped data of the class the plan sensors declare unrecorded and 1,684 B are byte-identical repeats of a (key, value) another entity published in the same cycle, so 36.1 % of the payload is avoidable by the project's own rule.
findings.mechanism: _unrecorded_attributes covers the plan sensors' series (forecast, slots, schedule, dhw_schedule) but not the series-shaped attributes of PredictiveInsightSensor (dhw_usage_profile, 481 B), ThermalBatterySensor (components, 470 B), DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor (candidates, 504 B) or SensorGapAdvisorSensor (gaps, 298 B); and six accumulating energy/cost sensors each publish their own copy of the same period and split_method values, byte-identical across all six.

evidence.unit: recorded attribute bytes per cycle over 64 entities (1,684 B/cycle duplicated, 1,753 B/cycle series-shaped)
evidence.contention_note: bytes: contention-immune; the fan-out box ran other finders (load1 3.18) and cannot move a byte count
evidence.tolerance: exact (deterministic fixtures, clock frozen at tests/golden.py START)
evidence.machine: Apple M1, 8 GB, darwin 25.6.0, audit box shared with other finders

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.sensor:HeatPumpOptimizerSensorBase.extra_state_attributes (with each subclass's _unrecorded_attributes, which HA's recorder filters on)

perturbation.change: add 'dhw_usage_profile' to PredictiveInsightSensor._unrecorded_attributes (the one-line production edit a fix makes)

findings.metric_definition: recorded attribute bytes per cycle: sum over every entity the platforms add of len(json.dumps(extra_state_attributes)) after removing that entity's unrecorded_attributes keys
findings.phenomenon_property: Every attribute an entity publishes outside its own unrecorded_attributes is written to the recorder on each state change; an attribute that is a series, or a byte-identical repeat of another entity's, is therefore a per-cycle write the project's own exclusion rule already rejects elsewhere.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round7/D9/payload_bytes.py --top 64 — enumerate every entity both platforms add and read its extra_state_attributes against its unrecorded_attributes

null_control.note: a key no entity publishes: recorded and excluded totals are byte-identical to the shipped arm, so the number is the payload and not the harness's own edit

findings.proposed_fix_scope: One pull request: add dhw_usage_profile, components, candidates and gaps to the respective entities' unrecorded_attributes (or drop them from the payload if the card reads them live), and publish period/split_method once instead of once per accumulating sensor. Leave-one-out: the recorded total with the largest single entity dropped is 8,415 B/cycle, so the finding does not rest on PredictiveInsightSensor alone.

findings.title: The per-candidate polish is 35 % of every solve's CPU and 37 % of its gradients
findings.claim: optimizer._lbfgsb_restart runs once per starting candidate and consumes 164 of the default two-zone DHW solve's 442 batched gradients (37.1 %) and 762.1 of its 2,170.4 ms CPU (35.1 %), against the code's own cost model of 'one short L-BFGS-B run per candidate, not a second solve'.
findings.mechanism: _multi_start_minimize polishes every scored candidate inside the loop (round-5 D0-02 / #1208) and hands each polish the same maxiter budget the main run got, so a polish is ~59 % of a main run's length (41 gradients against ~70) rather than a short one; four candidates means eight L-BFGS-B runs where four would do.

evidence.unit: CPU ms inside _lbfgsb_restart of a 2170.4 ms solve (share 0.3511, 40.216 reference solves)
evidence.contention_note: provisional: fan-out box, load1 4.00, thread_factor 1.000; the ratio against tests/stress.py:reference_solve and the gradient counts are the final half
evidence.tolerance: +/- 5 % on the share (two re-takes within 1.5 %); the counts are exact
evidence.machine: Apple M1, 8 GB, darwin 25.6.0, audit box shared with other finders

perturbation.change: return best at the top of _lbfgsb_restart (the one-line production edit that removes the polish)

findings.metric_definition: CPU ms inside optimizer._lbfgsb_restart and the batched gradients it runs, as a fraction of the whole optimize() CPU, over one default two-zone DHW solve
findings.phenomenon_property: A per-candidate polish that runs at the full restart budget is a second solver pass over the same candidates rather than a short refinement, and its cost is stated in the code as a short run.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round7/D9/polish_cost.py — one run per shape that calls _multi_start_minimize (two-zone DHW, two-zone space-only), each timing _lbfgsb_restart and the gradients that arrive inside it

null_control.note: the same instrument on the space-only shape (dhw=False), a different candidate set and no DHW stage: polish CPU share 0.3580, gradient share 0.3595, so the cost belongs to the polish and not to the DHW planner, which measures 93.3 ms / 4.3 % under the same instrument

findings.proposed_fix_scope: One pull request in optimizer.py: give the polish its own smaller maxiter (a short run, as the comment claims) or polish only the top-k candidates by score, and restate the measured share in the comment. Re-run tools/audit/round7/D9/polish_cost.py at both ends; the plan may move, so the golden may-drift path applies if a fixture moves.

findings.title: The cap/pin shapes still batch, and the work channel cannot tell the paths apart
findings.claim: tests/stress.py:1052-1058 states that a zero-range bound (power_cap_kw or pin_off_steps) 'takes the whole solve off the batched jacobian', but the fuse-cap shape build_case produces runs 316 batched gradients, and under the one-line edit that really does take it off, the gate's simulate_steps channel moves +0.019 % while the solve's CPU moves 16.1x.
findings.mechanism: D9-01 removed the fixed-variable carve-out from _bounds_supported_by_batch and moved the NaN case into _batch_fd_gradient, so no shipped bound shape refuses the batch; the sweep's cap and pin scenarios now sample the batched path, and the #1229 work channel charges a batch at rows x steps, which makes the two paths record the same step-equivalents for the same solve.

evidence.command: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round7/D9/gradient_cost.py --zero-range  # then the same harness with --scalar
evidence.value: batched_gradients 316 (zero-range) vs 0 (--scalar); simulate_steps 4128216 vs 4128984 (+0.019 %); kernel_ms 1238.1 vs 29807.9; solve_cpu_ms 2233.9 vs 35940.1
evidence.unit: counts (gradients, steps) plus CPU ms of one winter/2z/dhw solve
evidence.contention_note: provisional for the CPU ms (fan-out box, load1 4.30, thread_factor 1.000); the counts and the +0.019 % work delta are exact and contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: counts exact; the CPU ratio reproduced 16.1/16.4/16.1 across three re-takes
evidence.machine: Apple M1, 8 GB, darwin 25.6.0, audit box shared with other finders

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:_bounds_supported_by_batch, with optimizer:_batch_fd_gradient and tests/stress.py:SolverWork.simulate_steps counted at the same seam

perturbation.change: can_batch = False in _multi_start_minimize, i.e. optimizer._bounds_supported_by_batch returning False for every bound vector

findings.metric_definition: batched gradients = calls to optimizer._batch_fd_gradient per solve; work = scalar step calls plus rows x steps of simulate_trajectory_batch (stress.SolverWork.simulate_steps)
findings.phenomenon_property: Every bound shape the sweep builds is served by the batched finite-difference jacobian, and the gate's step-equivalent channel cannot distinguish a vectorized 96-row batch from 96 scalar trajectories, so any claim that keys on either must be re-derived by running the arm rather than read from the docstring or the budget.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round7/D9/gradient_cost.py --zero-range — one run per zero-range channel the sweep builds (power_cap_kw, pin_off_steps), plus --scalar as the arm where the batch is genuinely refused

null_control.note: the arm where the effect should vanish: no perturbation, the shipped batched path, 442 gradients and 4128216 step-equivalents against the scalar arm's 4128984 (+0.019 %) while the CPU differs 16.1x; on the zero-range shape the count is 316 against the docstring's 0

findings.proposed_fix_scope: One pull request, doc-and-instrument only: correct tests/stress.py's build_case docstring (the cap and pin shapes have sampled the batched path since D9-01, so the sweep no longer covers the scalar-FD path on either side of the change — add a scenario that does or retract the sentence), and state in SolverWork's docstring that simulate_steps cannot see a batched-vs-scalar swap while kernel_ms and the evaluation count can, so the work rule is not read as a cost rule.
